title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: U.S. exchanges are closed for the weekend; no new trading session since Friday's close. Nasdaq fell 2.1% Friday on AI-spending jitters (CoreWeave -11.9% on the day, >23% for the week), while the Dow still logged a weekly gain.
Markets: 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5.09%; Brent crude near $110/bbl (highest since May) on inflation/supply concerns; gold around $4,189/oz.
Companies: Tesla's flight-capable Roadster reveal got a cool reception (shares -2.1%); Barclays analysts flag a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger as soon as this fall, citing AI as a driver.
Companies: Apple and Meta struck a rare AI detente — Meta's 816B-parameter open-weight "Muse Spark Open" model will run locally on Apple's M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Macro/Policy: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no hint on an October move at IMF meetings in Bangkok; markets price ~17% odds of an Oct 27-28 hike (down from 28%), while AI-debt stress persists (CoreWeave selloff, stalled Firmus IPO, a stressed Oracle data-center loan, AI debt issuance down to $23B in Sept from $113B in June).
